The present study takes a closer look at the details of the event and attempts to portray the role that Astypalaia played in the raids of Catholic privateers against the Ottomans during the seventeenth century; raids which had become a regular occurrence because they could find provisions there (suc

the island and marriages between privateers and local Greek women), attest not only the strong relationship that the corsairs built with Astypalaia, but also the degree of appropriation of the place by them. In the last part of this study we examine the role of the bay of Vathy in the corsair raids, since this is most likely where the explosion of Creveliers' ship took place. This particular bay has similar traits to other anchorages in the Cycladic islands where we know that corsairs repaired their ships, since they had built small forts of batteries at the narrow entrances to these lairs so that no enemy ship could approach.
